note: Independent rejudgment 2026-11-24 against RFC 4760 Section 7 (rfc/full/rfc4760.txt): "If a BGP speaker receives from a neighbor an UPDATE message that contains the MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute, and if the speaker determines that the attribute is incorrect, the speaker MUST delete all the BGP routes received from that neighbor whose AFI/SAFI is the same as the one carried in the incorrect MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute." Verified changes since 9ab57ae45c (ba0f3a3a7d): TestRFC4760PeerDownDeletesOnlyThatNeighborsRoutes and TestHandleState_PeerDown migrated peer-table keying from IP address to PeerOwner ID with DestinationSession; both still assert the offender's PeerRIB is deleted on peer-down while a bystander neighbor's routes remain untouched. All message and reactor units (TestRFC4760IncorrectMPAttributeResetsTheSession, TestRFC4760IncorrectMPReachRaisesThePeerDownThatClearsTheRIB, TestRFC4760IncorrectMPReachDeletesTheNeighborsRoutes, TestRFC4760IncorrectMPUnreachDeletesTheNeighborsRoutes, and all three CorrectMPReach negatives) are unchanged and prove both the reset trigger and route deletion. Verdict stands: enforced.
